releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.19
releasesInRange.body:
pnpm 12.19.0 adds `pnpm fund`, lets the `loaded` node linker handle packages that need a build, and adds the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting and an experimental JSON lockfile format. It also includes a security fix: an offline install error no longer prints registry credentials. pnpm now checks the `engines` and platform fields of every workspace project, and many hoisted-linker and frozen-lockfile bugs are fixed.

### Minor Changes

- Added `pnpm fund`, which lists the funding URLs declared by the installed dependencies in the same tree `npm fund` prints. Use `--json` for the `npm fund --json` report and `--recursive` or `--filter` to report on workspace projects. `pnpm fund <pkg>` opens the funding URL of an installed package, and `--which` picks one when it lists several [#7354](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/7354).

- With `nodeLinker.type: loaded`, packages that need a build no longer have to be listed in `nodeLinker.excluded`. A package with a matching side-effects cache entry loads from the store. If side-effects cache reads and writes are enabled, pnpm builds an approved package once, saves the result to the side-effects cache, and then loads it from the store. This includes a build that changes no files in its package, so its script does not run again in other projects that use the same store. List a package in `sideEffectsCache.exclude` if its build must run in every project, such as a git hook installer. pnpm materializes other cache misses, packages with native `.node` addons, and their dependencies automatically.

  pnpm also scans JavaScript sources for filesystem imports and for `__dirname` or `import.meta`, and materializes matching packages. The scan does not detect computed imports. List such packages in `nodeLinker.excluded`.

- Added the `projectScopedOptionalPeers` setting. When it is `true`, a project gets a missing optional peer dependency only if the project's own dependencies install a version of it. Another workspace project's dependencies, such as its `devDependencies`, no longer supply one. `dedupePeerDependents` keeps deduplicating everything else [#16666](https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16666).

- Added the experimental `lockfile.format: v13` setting. With it, pnpm writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` in a JSON-like syntax, indented with tabs, with a trailing comma after every entry. The file is still valid YAML. The file has one `packages` entry per package version in place of the `packages` and `snapshots` sections, and each entry records the versions of its peer dependencies as its properties. Updating a peer dependency then changes only the lines that record its version. pnpm reads lockfiles in both formats whatever the setting is.

- `pnpm store add` now accepts directories of tarballs, such as `pnpm store add ./tarballs`, and adds every `.tgz`, `.tar.gz`, and `.tar` file inside them recursively. `pnpm store add` is now faster when it adds many packages or local tarballs [#17875](https://github.com/pnpm/pn
…(truncated)

fix(cmd-shim): switch code page without clearing the terminal
prs.author: HugStars
prs.body:
`chcp.com` clears the visible terminal on Windows whenever it changes the
console code page. The generated `.cmd` shims call it twice per run, so
`pnpm run` wiped the output of the script when the project path contained
non-ASCII characters.

Switch the shim's code-page calls to `mode.com con cp select=`, which changes
the same code page without clearing the screen, and use `mode.com con cp` for
the query. Trim the captured value because `mode.com` keeps the leading spaces
that `chcp.com` tolerated.

Closes #17899.

## Summary

`pnpm run` clears the visible terminal on Windows when the project path
contains non-ASCII characters. The generated `.cmd` shims switch the console
code page with `chcp.com` (added in #16205 for #6999), and `chcp.com` clears
the screen whenever it changes the code page (microsoft/terminal#9446). A shim
switches twice per run — UTF-8 before the target, the caller's code page
afterwards — so everything the script printed disappears.

This PR switches those calls to `mode.com con cp select=`, which changes the
same console code page without touching the screen. The query moves from
`chcp.com` to `mode.com con cp` too, because running `chcp.com` without
arguments also clears the terminal.

Closes #17899.

### Changes

- `pnpm/crates/cmd-shim/src/shim.rs` (v12 Rust):
  - `insert_utf8_codepage_switch` — query and switch
  - `CODEPAGE_RESTORE_TRAILER` — restore
  - `generate_batchless_cmd_shim` — restore on the last line

fix(fs-packlist): skip UUID-named lockfile staging files
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17824 ([review comment](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/17824#discussion_r4507780792) on `pnpm/crates/fs-packlist/src/lib.rs`).

`pnpm_fs_packlist::is_lockfile_staging_file` previously required the second dot-separated segment after `.pnpm-lock.yaml.` to consist only of ASCII digits, which matched pnpm v12's counter-based temporary lockfiles (`.pnpm-lock.yaml.<pid>.<counter>.tmp`) but missed pnpm v11's UUID-based temporary lockfiles (`.pnpm-lock.yaml.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`). If pnpm v11 writes a lockfile while pnpm v12 packs or fetches that package directory, a disappearing UUID-named staging file could cause the directory walk to fail on platforms where `DirEntry::file_type` falls back to `lstat`.

- Relax `is_lockfile_staging_file` to accept any non-empty identifier segment between `<pid>` and `.tmp`, matching the TypeScript `isLockfileStagingFile` predicate in `@pnpm/fs.packlist`.
- Add UUID-named lockfile staging file coverage to `pnpm-fs-packlist` and `pnpm-directory-fetcher` tests.
- The user-facing release note is already covered by the pending `.changeset/packlist-disappearing-entries.md` from pnpm/pnpm#17824.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Accept any non-empty identifier segment in `is_lockfile_staging_file`
so temporary lockfiles written by pnpm v11
(`.pnpm-lock.yaml.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`) are pruned alongside
numeric-counter staging files during directory walks.

Follow-up to pnpm/pnpm#17824.
```

prs.title: fix: record runtimeOnFail in the workspace state
prs.author: chinmayajha
prs.body:
## Summary

A repeat `pnpm install` ignored a `runtimeOnFail` change. Switching it from `ignore` to `download` printed "Already up to date" and the runtime from `devEngines.runtime` was never installed. Both v11 and v12 have it (reproduced with 11.22.0 and 12.18.0), so the fix is in both.

The workspace state now records `runtimeOnFail` when it is set, and the fast path compares it like the other recorded settings. The `pnpm run` deps check does not compare it, as it already does not compare `runtime`: a script runs with the runtime the last install linked, and an install that set `runtimeOnFail` only on the command line must not make `pnpm run` fail or reinstall without it.

Closes pnpm/tasks#303.

cc @zkochan

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The workspace state did not record runtimeOnFail, so the repeat-install
fast path could not see a change to it. Going from ignore to download
kept the old install, and the runtime a project declares in
devEngines.runtime was never added to the lockfile or linked.

Record runtimeOnFail in the workspace state when it is set (v11 adds it
to WORKSPACE_STATE_SETTING_KEYS, v12 to WorkspaceStateSettings, sharing
the RuntimeOnFail enum with pnpm-config, with the same lowercase values) and compare it with the install policy settings.
The run dependency check ignores it, as it ignores runtime.
A workspace that already sets runtimeOnFail runs one full install after
the upgrade, since older state files do not record it.

Closes pnpm/tasks#303.
```

prs.title: feat(lockfile): add an experimental next lockfile format
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

A prototype of the lockfile format proposed in pnpm/rfcs#72, behind an opt-in setting:

```yaml
lockfile:
  format: v13
```

With it, `pnpm-lock.yaml` is written as JSON, indented with tabs, with a trailing comma after every entry, which is valid YAML, so the file keeps its name and tools that read it as YAML still can, while pnpm reads it with a JSON parser. It has `lockfileVersion: '13.0'`, the number of the pnpm major planned to write the format by default, and one `packages` entry per package version, holding its metadata, its resolved dependencies, and one `peerDependencies` map with each declared peer's range beside the version it was bound to, and, marked `below: true`, the bindings a dependency below the package needed. Today's `transitivePeerDependencies` list is derived on read. `settings` holds everything recorded from `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: the resolution settings, `catalogs`, `overrides`, `patchedDependencies`, `ignoredOptionalDependencies` and the two checksums, so the top level is `lockfileVersion`, `settings`, `projects`, `packages` and `time`. There is no `snapshots` section. The tarball's `integrity` is a field of the entry, so a registry package has no `resolution` field. `peerDependenciesMeta` is folded into `peerDependencies`: an optional peer is `name: {specifier: range, optional: true}`. prs.title: fix(gvs): build global virtual store slots without locks
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The global virtual store was designed to work without locks: a slot's path is a hash of what it holds, so installs that share a slot write identical files. Builds broke that, because lifecycle scripts rewrite files inside the shared slot (pnpm/pnpm#15568). pnpm/pnpm#15634 serialized builds with a slot lock and a `started` marker. This PR removes the lock and the `.pnpm-needs-build` marker again, in both pnpm v11 and v12, and restores the lock-free design for builds:

- **A slot's package directory is final once its `package.json` exists.** Its files never change afterwards; only the shims in its `node_modules/.bin` are linked again, to the same targets.
- **Built and unbuilt packages never share a slot.** A slot whose package the install builds hashes an extra `built: true` field. An install under `ignoreScripts` leaves the field out, so it links the slots of unbuilt packages. The engine gating of the hash is unchanged.
- **Builds happen in private.** The link phase imports a package the install builds into a staging directory beside the slot's package directory (`.pnpm-<token>`, 32 random bits, short so a build's working directory stays within Windows' `MAX_PATH`). Its dependencies' bins are linked there, the build runs there, and the package is renamed into place. If another install placed it first, this install discards its copy. A package directory without `package.json` (an import that died) is replaced.
- **A failed build leaves nothing in the slot**, so no 
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(store): isolate and prune the directory clone cache
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Local installs on macOS now keep directory-clone materializations in a dedicated `dir-clone-cache` directory in the store. `pnpm store prune` clears this disposable cache under the store lock. Global virtual store packages keep their existing conservative reachability checks.

Pruning also stops on unexpected dependency-link read errors instead of sweeping an incomplete reachable set. This safety fix applies to both CLI implementations.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17907.

Existing entries in `links/` remain subject to global virtual store garbage collection. They cannot safely be classified as disposable cache entries because installed packages use the same layout and project registration is best-effort.

The disposable cache follows `storeDir`, so it requires the store and project to share a clone-capable volume. A custom `globalVirtualStoreDir` does not relocate this local-install cache. Frozen stores use per-file imports when the disposable cache is missing, including after upgrading a store whose cache was in `links/`.

prs.title: feat(lockfile): write the next format without blank lines between entries
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The experimental `lockfile.format: v13` lockfile no longer has a blank line between the entries of the top-level map and of `projects` and `packages`.

The blank lines came from the YAML format, where an entry could be a single line or end in an indented line directly followed by the next key, so a diff or a merge needed a separator. In the JSON syntax every entry is several lines and closes with its own `},` line. A three-way merge experiment over inserted and bumped neighbouring entries gives the same results with and without blank lines (`git merge-file` on five cases), and a single inserted entry diffs as one hunk either way. The 5,623-snapshot lockfile goes from 74,228 lines to 69,624; its bytes do not change after compression.

The format is unreleased, so there is no changeset. RFC amendment: pnpm/rfcs#73.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Every entry of the next format closes with its own `},` line, which gives a
diff or a merge the context the blank lines gave the YAML format. The
emitter writes entries without blank lines between them; the readers never
depended on them. The 5,623-snapshot lockfile goes from 74,228 lines to
69,624 and its bytes do not change.
```

prs.title: fix: apply version-selector overrides to catalog: dependencies
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes version-selector overrides (such as `"ms@^2.0.0": "2.1.1"` or `"parent>ms@^2.0.0": "2.1.1"`) not applying to dependencies declared with the `catalog:` protocol in both pnpm v12 (Rust) and pnpm v11 (TypeScript).

Unscoped overrides (`"ms": "2.1.1"`) already rewrote `"ms": "catalog:"` to `"2.1.1"` in `VersionsOverrider` / `createVersionsOverrider` because `is_intersecting_range(None, "catalog:")` short-circuited to `true`, whereas range-scoped overrides failed `Range::parse("catalog:")`. By dereferencing `catalog:` specifiers against the workspace `Catalogs` before testing range intersection, version-selector overrides apply to `catalog:` dependencies when the catalog entry's range intersects the selector's range (whether `catalogs` and `overrides` are configured in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or via an `updateConfig` hook). Convergence overrides (`"pkg@"`) continue to apply only to plain semver ranges as documented.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17922

## Squash Commit Body

```text
When matching a target package selector in VersionsOverrider (Rust)
and createVersionsOverrider (TypeScript), dereference catalog:
specifiers against the workspace catalogs before testing range
intersection so range-scoped overrides such as `pkg@^2.0.0` apply to
catalog-backed dependencies the same way unscoped overrides already do.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17922
```

prs.title: fix(pnpr): queue metadata writers on PostgreSQL and MySQL
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `database.url` on PostgreSQL or MySQL, concurrent publishes of distinct packages, and concurrent OCI blob uploads, failed with HTTP 500. PostgreSQL returned SQLSTATE 40001 ("could not serialize access"). MySQL returned error 1213 (deadlock). libSQL and SQLite were unaffected.

**Root cause.** A metadata write on a network database ran as a `SERIALIZABLE` transaction without any lock. SQLite and libSQL use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, which makes writers queue. Every commit in a catalog reads and advances the same `catalogs.generation` row and appends to the catalog's transparency log with `MAX(idx) + 1`. So two publishes of *different* packages always read and write a shared row:

- PostgreSQL's SSI aborts one of them. Blob mappings also conflict, because SSI's page-level predicate locks collide on distinct keys of small tables.
- MySQL's `SERIALIZABLE` turns the plain reads into shared locks. Both writers then try to upgrade them, which deadlocks.

The retry policy (4 attempts, 10 ms doubling) could not drain 8 or more concurrent writers.

**Fix.**

- A network write now takes a database-wide session lock (`pg_advisory_lock` / `GET_LOCK`, scoped to the database) **before** `BEGIN`, so the transaction's snapshot includes every commit made under the lock. The lock is released in the same round trip as `COMMIT` / `ROLLBACK`. If a write fails or times out, the cleanup path also releases it or closes the connection. Writers now queue the way they do on SQLite/libSQL, so th
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(pnpr): stop handing out expired libSQL streams
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With a remote libSQL `database.url` (self-hosted `sqld` or Turso) and no `replicaPath`, the first request on a pooled connection that sat idle for more than about 10 seconds failed with HTTP 500 (`STREAM_EXPIRED`), and with "Received an invalid baton" after `sqld` restarted. Login, whoami, package reads, and publish all hit it, and `/-/ping` and `/-/ready` answered 503, so an orchestrator would drain a healthy instance.

**Root cause.** A remote libSQL connection is a Hrana stream. `sqld` expires a stream 10 seconds after it last answered on it (`EXPIRATION` in libsql-server `hrana/http/stream.rs`), and a restarted `sqld` knows no baton. `ConnectionPool` reused idle connections with no age check. libsql keeps a stream open after a query, so the auth backend's token lookups and the readiness check left such streams in the pool. The metadata adapter is not affected: every operation ends with a `COMMIT`, which closes the stream.

**Fix** (`pnpr/crates/libsql/src/pool.rs`):

- An idle connection older than 5 seconds is closed instead of handed out. Opening a remote connection makes no request, since the first statement opens a new stream, so this adds no round trip to the hot path. Embedded-replica pools (`ConnectionPool::replica`) keep idle connections: they hold no stream, and opening one can wait for a background sync.
- When the server rejects a stream as stale, `read` and `write` run the operation once more on a new connection and close every idle connection. The
…(truncated)

prs.title: feat(pnpr): make the upstream tarball size limit configurable
prs.author: kelseyfrancis
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a `maxTarballSize` setting to pnpr's config file. It caps the size of a tarball pnpr fetches from an upstream registry and defaults to `100MiB`, the limit that was hard-coded until now, so nothing changes for a config that does not set it.

pnpr refuses an upstream tarball larger than the cap before streaming it (or mid-stream, when the upstream sends no `Content-Length`). The limit exists because pnpr spools every proxied tarball to a temporary file while it verifies the SRI integrity, so it bounds the disk one request can take. Until now the cap was the constant `MAX_TARBALL_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024` in `pnpr/crates/pnpr/src/server.rs`, with no way to change it.

Packages that ship large native binaries are now bigger than that. `onnxruntime-node` 1.30.0, pulled in transitively by `@huggingface/transformers` 4.3.x, has a 113,507,888-byte tarball, and the current release, 1.31.1, has a 115,391,311-byte one. Both are over the 104,857,600-byte cap, so a `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` that goes through pnpr fails on every run. pnpr logs:

```text
EINTEGRITY: tarball "onnxruntime-node-1.30.0.tgz" for package "onnxruntime-node": tarball body exceeds 104857600 byte limit (received 113507888 bytes)
```

pnpr answers the tarball request with 502, and pnpm gives up with `ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_HTTP_STATUS`. pnpm has no per-package fallback registry, so an install behind pnpr cannot complete at all. The only workaround is to pre-seed the pnpm store for the affected packa
…(truncated)

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:

`pnpr gc --dry-run` now excludes OCI image blobs from its removable set when another repository in the same organization still keeps them, either through a retained manifest or through a recent upload within `--min-age`.

fix: bundle node-gyp with undici 7
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The bundled node-gyp 12 depends on undici `^6.25.0`. Scanners flag undici 6 for CVE-2026-84947, and no undici 6 release has the fix. This PR overrides node-gyp 12's undici to the catalog's undici 7 (7.30.1, already in the lockfile). node-gyp 12 was the only package resolving undici 6.

Both the v11 (`pnpm11/pnpm`) and v12 (`pnpm/npm/pnpm`) packages deploy their bundled node-gyp from the workspace lockfile, so this covers both.

node-gyp only imports `EnvHttpProxyAgent` from undici and passes it as the dispatcher to the global `fetch`. I ran node-gyp's `lib/download.js` against a local CONNECT proxy and also with a `cafile`:

| | Node 22.19 | Node 24.6 | Node 26.13 |
|---|---|---|---|
| undici 6.29.1 (before) | ok | ok | crash: `invalid onError method` |
| undici 7.30.1 (after) | ok | ok | ok |

So the override also fixes node-gyp downloads through a proxy or with a custom CA on Node.js 26.

undici 7 reads the global `File` when it loads, and Node.js 18, which pnpm 12 supports, has none. `.config/pnpm/patches/node-gyp@12.3.0.patch` sets `globalThis.File` from `buffer` before node-gyp loads undici. With the rebuilt bundle, proxy and CA-file downloads pass on Node.js 18.20.8, 20.16.0, 22.13.0 and 26.13.0, and `node-gyp install` downloads headers on Node.js 18. `pnpm run bundle-node-gyp` now ships `dist/node_modules/undici` 7.30.1.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17941

prs.title: fix(pnpr): read primary on embedded-replica archive and version misses
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With an embedded libSQL `replicaPath`, fetching a newly published tarball, archive, or exact version on a second pnpr instance before its `syncInterval` elapsed answered HTTP 404. While stale packuments and listings within `syncInterval` are expected and documented, a client that resolved the packument on the publishing instance and then fetched the tarball from an unsynced replica failed the install.

**Root cause.** `PackageMetadata::artifact_blob`, `read_version`, `read_release_record`, `SqlMetadata::release_record_entry`, `SqlMetadata::publication`, and exact-version / archive lookups inside hosted documents all ran as `Freshness::Bounded` reads against the local replica, and `SqlMetadata` did not retry a miss on the primary.

**Fix:**

- `pnpr_sql::Adapter::read` now returns `Snapshot::{Current, Lagging}`. `LibsqlAdapter` returns `Snapshot::Lagging` only when reading an already-cached local replica (`replica.is_fresh()` before the read); reads on the primary, reads that ran `replica.sync` during the call, and non-replica adapters (`Sqlite`, `Postgres`, `Mysql`, remote-only `Libsql`) return `Snapshot::Current`.
- `SqlMetadata::read_if` and `SqlMetadata::read_present` run on the replica first and retry on the primary only when a `Snapshot::Lagging` read misses. Warm replica hits, freshly synced reads, and non-replica backends make no extra primary round trip.
- Switched `artifact_blob` (covering npm `.tgz` tarballs, `<pkg>@<version>` tarballs, hosted `tar` regi
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix: read current registry metadata before package mutations
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Use `?write=true` when reading package metadata for `deprecate`, `undeprecate`, and `unpublish` in both CLIs. This requests the current document revision before a write and avoids conflicts caused by stale registry caches. Unpublish's follow-up reads before tarball deletion use the same query.

Dist-tag mutations use dedicated endpoints and do not write a packument revision, so they do not need this change.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/57

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Request write metadata before mutating a registry package document in both
CLIs. Keep the query on GET requests so PUT and DELETE endpoints retain
their existing paths. Reuse the shared Rust metadata reader to cover
deprecate, undeprecate, and every unpublish revision refresh.

Require write=true in registry mocks, including scoped package paths,
registry path prefixes, and the refresh before deleting tarballs.

Recent fixes in this area addressed command headers, response size limits,
and registry URL construction. They did not address revision freshness;
this fix extends the existing metadata reader rather than adding another.

Closes https://github.com/zkochan/pnpm-tasks/issues/57
```
